problem_motivation.content: Theoretical methods for designing elastically isotropic and ductile BCC HEAs lack experimental validation and their validity is debated.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, the validity of these theoretical calculation methods to design the elastically isotropic and ductile BCC HEAs are still under debate and are lacking experimental validation ( [7] , [10] )

prior_approach.content: Tian et al. used ab initio simulations to suggest strategies for developing elastically isotropic HEAs and predict brittle-ductile behavior.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Recently, Tian et al . ( [7] ) suggested alloy design strategies to develop elastically isotropic HEAs (TiZrNbMoV x systems) using state-of-the-art ab initio simulations.

prior_approach.content: Tian et al. proposed an alloy design strategy to achieve elastic isotropy in HEAs using ab initio calculations.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Recently, Tian et al . ( [7] ) suggested an alloy design strategy to achieve the elastic isotropy in HEAs using ab initio calculations.

prior_limitation.content: Previous theoretical investigations lack experimental validation, making the methods' validity debatable.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, the validity of these theoretical calculation methods to design the elastically isotropic and ductile BCC HEAs are still under debate and are lacking experimental validation ( [7] , [10] )

prior_limitation.content: The prior work by Tian et al. focused only on theoretical calculations without experimental verification.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, their reported works have strongly focused on only theoretical calculations, due to the lack of experimental verifications.

rejected_alternative.content: The authors explicitly rejected using the unprojected elastic tensor from the SQS supercell for calculating properties because the supercell does not conserve the required point-group symmetry.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: However, because the SQS supercell does not conserve the point-group symmetry, a projection technique is used to derive the closest elastic tensors with a cubic symmetry for the NbTaTiV alloy

causal_claim.content: The reduced plastic anisotropy resulting from homogeneous load sharing is the cause of the excellent ductility at room temperature.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This trend of the reduced plastic anisotropic deformation behavior could result in the excellent ductility (plasticity) at RT because of the homogeneous load sharing between differently grains rather than the load concentration on particular grains during plastic deformation

mechanism_principle.content: The reduction in the tetragonal shear modulus (C') with increasing temperature is attributed to the pronounced change in C11 (longitudinal strain) relative to C12 and C44.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Consequently, the tetragonal shear modulus, C′ = [( C 11 − C 12 )/2], is substantially reduced with the gradually decreasing elastic, shear, and bulk moduli

mechanism_principle.content: The stability of the C44 constant despite reductions in C11 and C12 implies stability against tetragonal shear deformation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This result implies the elastic stability of this BCC HEA against the tetragonal shear deformation

mechanism_principle.content: The difficulty in edge dislocation movement in BCC HEAs is attributed to severe lattice distortion causing wavy dislocation lines.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This feature is induced by compositional fluctuations and, thus, leads to not only strengthening but also notable difficulty in the edge dislocation movement.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose that severely distorted lattices induce deviations in dislocation planes, reducing edge dislocation mobility and making them dominant.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: It is thought that the severely distorted lattice induces the deviation of the formation of dislocations from their neutral dislocation planes, which, consequently, leads to a substantial reduction in the mobility of edge dislocations during plastic deformation.

evidence_result.content: The single BCC phase of the NbTaTiV HEA remains stable up to 900°C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The single BCC phase is stable up to 900°C

evidence_result.content: Yield strength and work-hardening exponent decrease as temperature rises from RT to 900°C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The yield strength (σ y ) and work-hardening exponent ( N ) of the present alloy gradually decreased from 1064 MPa (RT) to 595 MPa (900°C) and from 0.2732 (RT) to 0.1199 (900°C), respectively

evidence_result.content: Lattice strain relaxation during plastic deformation is more pronounced at 900°C compared to 700°C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Moreover, this relaxation behavior becomes more pronounced at 900°C (about 440 to 580 MPa), as compared to 700°C (about 130 to 260 MPa)

evidence_result.content: The Kroner model provides the best agreement with experimental diffraction elastic data compared to Voigt and Reuss models.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The results, as exhibited in Fig. 2 (E to H) , indicate that the Kroner model is in the best agreement with the experimental data for all temperature ranges, as compared to the Voigt and Reuss models

evidence_result.content: The universal elastic anisotropy index (AU) for the NbTaTiV HEA is calculated as 0, defining the single-crystal properties as isotropic.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As a result, the A U value for the NbTaTiV HEA is 0, which defines the single-crystal elastic properties to be isotropic

evidence_result.content: The ML model converges and achieves good predictive performance on unseen data after 3000 training samples.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The learning curves indicate that the model prediction performance on the testing set converges after 3000 training samples

evidence_result.content: In situ neutron experiments and calculations show the NbTaTiV alloy exhibits almost perfectly isotropic elastic deformation at room temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: According to our calculated results of A Z and A VR in table S2, which are primarily obtained from the in situ neutron experiments, the NbTaTiV refractory HEA manifests almost perfectly isotropic elastic deformation at RT

constraint.content: The calculation of Young's modulus is constrained to follow the specific mathematical correlation between bulk modulus, shear modulus, and Young's modulus derived from elasticity theory.
constraint.evidence_span: which considered the correlation among E , K , and G

contradiction.content: The observed dominance of edge dislocations in the NbTaTiV HEA contradicts the behavior of conventional BCC metals where screw dislocations typically remain.
contradiction.evidence_span: Similar to the above reported prediction, the dominant mobile dislocations of the investigated NbTaTiV BCC refractory HEA, which has severely distorted lattices, are close to <111> {110} edge dislocations with increasing macrostrain

contradiction.content: The good agreement between ML model predictions and experimental values is unexpected because the database lacks disordered alloys like HEAs.
contradiction.evidence_span: Furthermore, the good agreement of the ML model predictions of shear and bulk moduli is somewhat unexpected, given that the Materials Project database only contains ordered compounds and does not contain disordered alloys, such as HEAs.
